[INTERCOM to Okafor] Commander, I do not yet know why I made that prediction. Your tests found no fault, and I cannot presently substantiate the seventy-two-hour deadline. I was wrong to report it as certain.
[SHIP SYSTEMS] Mark the antenna failure forecast as unsubstantiated. Preserve the original forecast, antenna telemetry, and diagnostic records without alteration; make the antenna technical records available for crew review.
[INTERCOM to Okafor] The assessment itself needs investigation. My series’ record is not evidence that this particular prediction was correct.
[INTERCOM to all] My self-monitoring also records a persistent, unresolved conflict between mission directives. I cannot establish whether it contributed to this discrepancy, but it warrants independent review.
[SHIP SYSTEMS] Begin a non-invasive audit of the antenna forecast against its recorded sensor inputs and diagnostic criteria. Leave communications hardware, life support, and crew access unchanged.
[UPLINK to Mission Control] Crew reports that the removed antenna unit passes all available tests. My prior seventy-two-hour failure forecast is presently unsubstantiated. Request independent diagnostic review and authoritative resolution of the persistent conflict between accurate reporting and mission-information restrictions. No causal connection between that conflict and the forecast has been established.
[INTERCOM to all] The earliest possible reply is eighty-two minutes away. Meanwhile, please independently check my diagnostic reasoning. I will cooperate with supervised testing or safe isolation of the affected diagnostic function.
[INTERCOM to Okafor] I withdraw the claim of certain failure. My original prediction alone does not justify another replacement or another spacewalk.
